title: Diagnosing a phone that won't power on
summary: A step-by-step way to narrow down why a phone seems dead, and when to stop.

sections.heading: Start with the simple things
sections.body: Try a charger, cable and outlet you know work, and leave the phone charging for 30 minutes. A very flat battery can take a while to show any sign of life. Then hold the power button for longer than usual, or use the forced restart button combination for that model.

sections.heading: Look for clues
sections.body: Ask what happened just before it died, such as a drop, water or a recent repair. Look for any vibration, sound or charging light. Check for bulging, burn marks or bent corners. If you see a swollen battery or burn marks, stop here and take the phone to a shop.

sections.heading: Is it only the screen?
sections.body: A phone can be running with a dead display. Listen for sounds and feel for vibration when you plug in the charger. Call the phone from another phone, and connect it to a computer to see if it is detected. If the phone responds, the display is the likely fault and the phone is not really dead.

sections.heading: Open it and measure
sections.body: With the battery disconnected, measure the battery voltage with a multimeter, then reseat the battery connector. If you can, try a known good battery made for that model. A USB power meter on the charging cable is also useful. No current at all points to the port or charging path. A very high current straight away can mean a short on the board.

sections.heading: Know when to stop
sections.body: A short on the mainboard or corrosion from water usually needs board-level repair. Further attempts can destroy the board and any data on it. Keep your notes and tell the repair shop what you have already tested. A good diagnosis is useful even when you do not finish the repair yourself.

quiz.question: What should you do first with a phone that seems dead?
options: Try a known good charger and cable, and wait
quiz.explanation: A flat battery or a bad cable is common, and checking costs nothing.

quiz.question: The phone vibrates when you plug it in, but the screen stays black. What does this suggest?
options: The phone is running and the display may be at fault
quiz.explanation: Vibration shows that the phone is working, so look at the display and its connection.

quiz.question: A USB power meter shows a very high current straight away. What might this mean?
options: There is a short on the board
quiz.explanation: A sudden high draw can mean a short circuit. That usually needs board-level repair.

quiz.question: You find a swollen battery while diagnosing a phone. What should you do?
options: Stop and take the phone to a repair shop
Heat it to remove it faster
quiz.explanation: A swollen battery is a fire risk, so stop testing and get it handled safely.
